knowledge:
- key_parameters: pfamResultFile=The path to the Pfam prediction result text file (from webserver or stand-alone runs) passed as the primary argument to pfamAnalyzeR()
- alternatives: None mentioned
- when_to_use: When analyzing transcriptomics or proteomics data with Pfam domain predictions to identify and classify domain isotypes (e.g., to study cell-, tissue-, or disease-specific domain variants)
- pitfalls: The isotype analysis is performed regardless of the Pfam result type (Domain, Family, Repeat); users interested in only a specific annotation type must manually subset the output table themselves

workflows.name: pfam_domain_isotype_analysis
workflows.intent: Read Pfam domain prediction results and classify them into domain isotypes.
input: pfam_results.txt (Pfam prediction output file from webserver or stand-alone run)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the pfamAnalyzeR library ;; 2. Define the path to the Pfam result file ;; 3. Run the isotype classification analysis using pfamAnalyzeR() ;; 4. Explore and summarize the results using dplyr and base R table functions
workflows.code:
library(pfamAnalyzeR)
pfamResultFile <- system.file(
    "extdata/pfam_results.txt",
    package = "pfamAnalyzeR"
)
pfamRes <- pfamAnalyzeR(pfamResultFile)
pfamRes %>% 
    select(seq_id, hmm_name, type, domain_isotype, domain_isotype_simple) %>% 
    head()
table(pfamRes$domain_isotype)
table(pfamRes$domain_isotype_simple)
table(
    pfamRes$type,
    pfamRes$domain_isotype_simple
)
